summary:
Med-Point is an innovative, interactive and intuitive web application whose primary incentive is to provide a user-friendly interface (a dashboard) that demonstrates all particular health statistics for each astronaut. Many astronauts lack an easily accessible health monitoring system in space, since most health apps for tailored for users on Earth. As such, we have included a recommendation system for potentially critical health stats, as well as diagrams to represent how these statistics evolved over time in space. We also added daily tasks to ensure astronauts are actively motivated to track these statistics. 
In terms of this app's importance, it can be noted that space naturally has long-term effects on the human body, and not having instantaneous access to Earth during a specialized mission means that it is difficult to keep track of these conditions at all times. While there is a wide variety of health-oriented apps, this one is focused on the specific statistics that are most important for crew onboard a mission in space, including:
Body mass index
Average heart rate
Blood pressure
Muscle mass percentage
Body fat percentage
Stress level
Mission radiation exposure limit
Bone density (calcium)
Blood glucose
Sleep duration. 
Additionally, viewing other crew members is intuitive and allows for intercommunication.
details:
Med-Point is a web application for monitoring astronaut health during space missions. Its dashboard brings crew health measurements, historical trends, and informational recommendations together in one place, helping users follow changes that can be difficult to monitor when a crew is far from Earth.

Features

  • Crew dashboard: Review astronauts in a crew and switch between their health profiles.
  • Health metrics: Track body mass index (BMI), average heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, muscle mass, body fat, stress, mission radiation exposure, bone density (calcium), blood glucose, and sleep duration.
  • Health history: View measurement history and trends when data is available.
  • Recommendations: See informational health recommendations based on recorded measurements, with support for mission-phase context.
  • Daily tracking checklist: See which health measurements have been recorded for the selected astronaut today. Checklist status is based on the measurement history; it is not a form for entering measurements.
  • Visual dashboard: Explore health information alongside an interactive astronaut model and crew overview.
  • Accounts: Create an account, join or form a crew, sign in, and sign out.

Technology

  • HTML for dashboard, sign-in, and registration pages
  • CSS for the responsive interface and dashboard components
  • JavaScript for charts, crew and astronaut navigation, metric filters, recommendations, and the 3D model
  • Python / Flask for the web application, account flows, and JSON endpoints
  • SQLite / SQL for astronaut profiles, accounts, and measurement history

Creativity factor

  • 3D rendering is innovative and shows a very succinct albeit visual representation of health conditions
  • Graphs demonstrate how these statistics evolved over time
  • Quick management of crew members
